crop.notes: Whole Wray's Column in its two columns; the Allen section ('The Champion's Rest' and 'Did He Maintain Order!') is complete.

ocr.notes: The Allen part is mostly right, but there are errors: 'head and gavel in hand' should be 'skull cap on his bald head and gavel in hand'; 'a handlebar mustache and a heavy hand' is dropped; 'six rounds' should be 'four rounds'. The second column (Routis, Sarron, Armstrong) is left out entirely.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch's Wray's Column recalled Tom Allen as the only St. Louis resident to claim a world title, beating Mike McCoole in 1873, and described the ring and piano in the back room of his Champion's Rest saloon.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Friday, October 29, 1937, page 2C. The column says Allen died in 1904; he died in 1903.

facts.fact: In the 1869 championship match with Mike McCoole, Allen won the fight, but the referee, intimidated by McCoole's backers and a mob, gave the decision to McCoole
Four years later Allen beat McCoole in seven rounds on an island in the Mississippi and regained the championship
places: island in the Mississippi River, near St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen held the title until beaten by Joe Goss, then retired and renamed his saloon on Market Street east of Seventh the "Champion's Rest"
places: Market Street east of Seventh, St. Louis

facts.fact: Behind the saloon was a large back room with a ring in one corner and a piano platform in another; Allen sat by the doorway with a gavel as master of ceremonies and bouncer, and noisy disputants were gloved up and put in the ring to fight it out
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis

notes: Retrospective column (1937), mainly about Henry Armstrong vs. Petey Sarron. Its facts are secondhand, hence medium confidence. The current summary is wrong: it says Allen took the title from McCoole in 1869 and mentions Jem Mace, who is not in this article.
